color_space_note: All colour triplets are linear scene-referred RGB, not sRGB hex.

world_coordinate_convention.purpose: Stable world-space convention every WEB-HERO-001 phase must share, so Phase C/D can extend the camera path and inject AOI geometry without a scene reset.
world_coordinate_convention.up_axis: world +Z is Earth's rotation axis (geographic north)
world_coordinate_convention.reference_orientation: At frame 1 of hero_earth_orbit, geographic longitude 0 deg / latitude 0 deg sits on world +X. Earth spins about +Z (see the earth object's rotation_keyframes). Longitude increases counter-clockwise viewed from +Z, matching standard right-handed spherical-to-Cartesian conversion.
world_coordinate_convention.note: WEB-HERO-001C/D must place AOI geometry, scan beams and any further camera moves in this same frame/scale/orientation; do not introduce a second convention.

aoi_injection_interface.purpose: Single configuration surface for AOI geometry. WEB-HERO-001C reads footprint geometry only from here, and WEB-005 replaces the design fixtures below with accepted AOI geometry and rendered scientific layers without touching scene or builder code.
aoi_injection_interface.texture_longitude_offset_note: Fallback longitude offset aligning configured coordinates with the Earth equirectangular texture. A scene that defines an earth_day_night material overrides this with that material's texture_rotation_deg, so the AOI follows any re-framing of the globe instead of drifting off its configured coordinates.

schema.center_lat_deg: required. Footprint centre latitude, degrees north.
schema.center_lon_deg: required. Footprint centre longitude, degrees east.
schema.span_km: required. Edge length of the square footprint, kilometres of surface arc.
schema.bearing_deg: optional, default 0. Rotation of the footprint about its own surface normal.
schema.surface_offset_m: optional, default 250. Anti-z-fighting offset above the Earth radius; visual only.
schema.edge_samples: optional, default 48. Slerp samples per footprint edge; controls how finely the border follows curvature.
schema.fill_grid: optional, default 24. Interior grid resolution per axis; also the AOI-local (u, v) sweep parameter space.
schema.border_width_km: optional, default 14. Width of the border ribbon, kilometres of surface arc.
schema.corner_lock_arm_km: optional, default 70. Length of each corner-lock arm along the adjacent edge.
schema.corner_lock_width_km: optional, default 9. Width of the corner-lock arm ribbon.
schema.corner_lock_offset_m: optional, default 400. Extra radial offset for corner locks so they read above the border.

design_primary.label: Design fixture A
design_primary.note: Design placeholder with no measurement meaning. The deliberately round coordinates and span were chosen only so the footprint sits on the lit, camera-facing hemisphere at this phase's shot scale; they name no site, survey or project and carry no scientific claim.

design_secondary.label: Design fixture B
design_secondary.note: Second design placeholder, also carrying no measurement meaning. It exists to prove configurability: a different centre, span, bearing and sampling density must flow through the same code path with no scene or builder change. Southern hemisphere and rotated on purpose, so a hand-modelled footprint could not pass for it.

kizildere_regional.label: Kizildere regional acquisition frame
kizildere_regional.note: Production framing for the hero acquisition shot. The centre is the real accepted Kizildere pilot centre (37.9794 N, 28.7907 E), so the hero targets the real pilot area instead of a placeholder. The 420 km span is the REGIONAL ACQUISITION FRAME the accepted WEB-HERO-001D camera path was derived against -- it is a framing extent and carries no measurement meaning. The accepted analysis AOI is 36 x 36 km and is never claimed to be this box: is_analysis_aoi is false, and public copy states the 36 km extent separately. WEB-005A thinned the border and corner locks and raised the edge sampling for render fidelity; the centre, span, bearing and surface offset -- everything that carries geometric meaning -- are unchanged.

kizildere_analysis.label: Kizildere analysis AOI (36 x 36 km)
kizildere_analysis.centre_provenance: assets/imagery/sources.json -> geo_web_002.context_scenes[kizildere-aoi-context-2025]; span from geo_web_002.assets[*].grid (1200 x 1200 cells at 30 m)
kizildere_analysis.bearing_note: UTM zone 35 grid convergence at the centre, gamma = (28.7907 - 27) * sin(37.9794 deg) = 1.10 deg: the accepted EPSG:32635 grid square's north edge lies 1.10 deg east of true north, so the frame is turned by that much to sit on the accepted grid. Presentation registration only; nothing is measured from it.
kizildere_analysis.note: WEB-005A R3: the accepted 36 x 36 km analysis AOI itself, drawn as the frame the regional hold resolves onto so the page-layer analytical result can be registered inside it. It is the same accepted centre as kizildere_regional and the accepted grid extent; it carries no measurement meaning of its own and no scientific layer is rendered into it -- the governed rasters arrive as HTML overlays registered to this frame's audited screen corners.

layer_slots.mandatory_warning: AOI-relative experimental screening only. Not probability, reserve/resource estimation, discovery likelihood, drilling-success likelihood, Full Prospectivity, or a calibrated cross-AOI score.
layer_slots.render_surface_reason: A governed class-B raster must not be recoloured, value-transformed or re-encoded. Lossy video compression would do all three, so the accepted derivative is shipped as its exact checksummed file and composited over the video in the page instead of baked into a frame. This also keeps acquisition imagery and analytical result visibly distinct.

aoi_injection_interface.note: WEB-005 integration. The two design fixtures are untouched and still carry no measurement meaning. layer_slots now declares the one accepted result layer the hero hands off to, including the surface it is rendered on; nothing scientific is baked into the render.
aoi_injection_interface.classification_note: The two design fixtures below stay exactly as accepted at WEB-HERO-001D and remain classified design_fixture. WEB-005 adds one production fixture carrying real accepted geometry; each fixture now declares its own classification.

benchmark_neutral.description: Minimal neutral pipeline benchmark: camera, primitive geometry, two lights, dark world. Lit to sit in the restrained dark/high-dynamic-range regime the hero scene will actually render in, so the timing is representative. Exists to measure render throughput, not to express hero art direction.

hero_earth_orbit.description: WEB-HERO-001B establishing sequence: true 3D Earth with day/night material and atmosphere shell, a procedurally-modelled Earth-observation satellite entering along a plausible orbital arc, deep-space starfield background. Pre-data: no AOI or scientific layer is rendered here.

hero_aoi_acquisition.description: WEB-HERO-001C acquisition sequence. Inherits the accepted WEB-HERO-001B Earth, atmosphere, satellite, starfield and lighting unchanged, then extends the single continuous camera move from global establish through acquisition into regional approach and adds the surface-conforming AOI system. Pre-data: the footprint interior carries a neutral cyan scan treatment only and no scientific layer.

animation.continuity_note: Frames 1-120 reuse the WEB-HERO-001B camera keyframes verbatim, so this shot continues the accepted establish rather than restating it. The AOI is one object system present for the whole range; it is never recentred, re-parented or rebuilt, and the move from global to regional is camera motion only.

objects.note: One persistent AOI system parented to the Earth, so the footprint, its corner locks and the beam target points stay registered through Earth rotation and the whole camera move.

hero_predata_animatic.description: WEB-HERO-001D continuous pre-data animatic. Inherits the accepted Phase-B Earth, satellite and starfield and the accepted Phase-C surface-conforming AOI acquisition system unchanged, and assembles them into one uninterrupted 240-frame move: Earth establish, satellite entrance, AOI acquisition and scan, continuous camera approach, stable regional AOI hold. Phase-D work is assembly, timing and the three accepted Phase-C quality-gate items only: an 8192 px albedo for closest-approach sharpness, an additive perigee-altitude atmosphere replacing the Fresnel hoop, and a constraint-locked camera aim. The inherited atmosphere_shell material is left defined and unreferenced on purpose, so the accepted Phase-C shell is visibly untouched rather than edited in place. Pre-data: no scientific layer exists anywhere in it.

animation.continuity_note: One scene, one world, one camera, no cut. Frames 1-96 replay the three accepted Phase-B establish camera states verbatim, re-timed onto this beat map so acquisition can start earlier and the shot can end on a real hold; every keyframe from 136 on is derived from the AOI itself by hero/scripts/shot_plan.py rather than typed by eye. The AOI is one object system present for the whole range, never recentred, re-parented or rebuilt.

composition.note: Website copy is never baked into the render, so what the opening owes the later integration task is empty sky. This rectangle is a left-aligned headline and CTA column, 33 percent of the frame width by 62 percent of its height; shot_plan.py casts a ray through a 28x28 grid of it at every establish keyframe and reports the frame as failed if any ray hits the Earth. It was measured, not guessed: the region was widened until the planet first intruded, then stepped back to the last width that stays completely clear through frame 96.

track.note: Precision lock, not a redirect. The derived keyframes from 136 on already aim at the AOI centre, so the constraint changes nothing at a key; it removes the drift that appears between keys because the footprint travels an arc on a rotating planet while an interpolated camera aims along a chord.

atmosphere_limb.note: Single shell at 6.85 BU, 479 km of headroom above the surface. The glow is driven by the perigee altitude of each view ray and decays with a 55 km scale height, so it is already about two parts in ten thousand at the shell boundary and the shell has no visible edge. grazing_exponent confines on-disc haze to near-grazing sightlines.

hero_production_kizildere.description: WEB-005A R3 production hero. Consumes the accepted WEB-HERO-001D world, camera establish and surface-conforming AOI system over the real accepted Kizildere regional frame, and revises the visual treatment to the Product R2 lock as re-reviewed: a volumetric generic EO satellite on a time-remapped derived orbit that comes round the limb fast and settles lower-left of the target for the whole acquisition beat; thin cyan sensing lines that connect, hold through a visible sweep and release while the platform is still in frame; a crisp target frame with corner locks and a lock pulse; a continuous dive from the acquisition composition down to a 170 km regional hold in which the accepted 36 x 36 km analysis AOI resolves as the frame the page-layer analytical result is registered into; and a Blue Marble albedo carrying 30 m Sentinel-2 ground structure under the hold. No scientific layer is baked into any frame, and no accepted geometry, public label or claim changes.

animation.continuity_note: One scene, one world, one camera, no cut. R3 re-times the shot around a satellite that settles: the platform comes round the limb, is readable by frame 80 and holds lower-left through the lock (128-144) and the sweep (144-178) while the camera is locked off; the lines release at 178-192 with the platform still in frame; and only then does the camera make one decisive dive (192-262) onto the analysis AOI, whose frame draws in at 236-254 with its own lock pulse as the regional frame vanishes. The hold from 262 is what the page hands off from; the poster is the last frame.

shot_intent.note: Locked-off acquisition composition: from the handover to the release the camera only creeps, so the satellite can hold its place on screen while it works.

Regional hold: about 170 km of ground across the frame at 27 deg incidence, so the 36 km analysis AOI spans about 23 percent of the width and reads nearly square. The camera stays above the atmosphere shell. The state is reached at 262 and repeated at 276 so the hold is genuinely still.

composition.note: Website copy is never baked into the render, so what the opening owes the later integration task is empty sky. This rectangle is a left-aligned headline and CTA column, 33 percent of the frame width by 62 percent of its height; shot_plan.py casts a ray through a 28x28 grid of it at every establish keyframe and reports the frame as failed if any ray hits the Earth. It was measured, not guessed: the region was widened until the planet first intruded, then stepped back to the last width that stays completely clear through frame 96.

satellite_readability.note: At the primary acquisition frame the satellite must span at least 7.5 percent of the frame width (about 108 px at 1440 CSS px) so body and arrays read as a 3D platform, and never more than 20 percent anywhere in the visible pass, so it cannot become the foreground fly-by the rejected checkpoint's predecessor produced.

composition.aoi_anchor_note: After the handover the AOI sits at the shifted anchor, not frame centre; audit_shot.py checks the lock against (0.5 - shift_x, 0.5 - shift_y * width/height) per frame.
composition.acquisition_beat_note: The primary acquisition beat, R3: sensing lines connect at 110-124, the frame locks at 128-144, the sweep runs 144-178 and the lines release at 178-192 -- and the satellite holds lower-left of the target, fully in frame, through all of it while the camera barely moves. The audit gates clipping, side, overlap and size over exactly this window.

analysis_hold.note: From this frame the accepted 36 km analysis AOI must span between 19 and 26 percent of the frame width and stay there: wide enough for the governed rasters to read as the payoff, narrow enough that a 2x display at 2560 CSS px keeps them under the 1249 device-pixel ceiling without shrinking inside the frame.

track.note: Unchanged accepted precision lock, held through the extended rest.

camera.shift_note: Lens shift, not a re-aim: the AOI track constraint holds the target on the optical axis and the shift places that axis in the frame (x = 0.5 - shift_x, y = 0.5 - shift_y * 16/9). Through the acquisition beat the target sits upper right (0.70, 0.66) with the Earth right-dominant and the headline column clear; through the dive it eases to (0.63, 0.55), where the analysis frame lands with room for the page-layer caption column to its right. Zero through the accepted establish.

corner_locks.exit_note: The regional corner locks are not faded: as the camera dives they sweep outward and leave past the frame edges by frame 250, which reads as the acquisition frame opening onto the analysis AOI. Only the border, halo and fill vanish (presence-gated).

objects.note: The regional acquisition frame (420 km), parented to the Earth so footprint, corner locks and sensing-line targets stay registered through Earth rotation and the whole camera move. R3: four thin core lines to the corners inside glow sheaths plus one faint support cone; a crisp border with a soft halo ribbon; corner locks that draw in; a lock pulse at 134-160 and an acquisition-complete pulse at 196 as the lines release; a visible sweep band 148-186; and a vanish under the dive (238-254) as its edges leave the frame and the analysis frame takes over.

WEB-005A R2/R3 generic EO platform (hero/scripts/satellite_model.py): volumetric bus in MLI with structural end frames and a radiator, a nadir instrument deck with two apertures, two three-segment arrays with real thickness on yokes, a small dish, star trackers and a thruster. Rights-clean by construction and the signature of no operational spacecraft. Hero-scale, like the accepted model: R3 raises the wingspan to 1.15 BU so the platform is readable where it now holds, out at the limb and farther from the camera than the R2 pass put it.

aim.note: Off-nadir slew toward the footprint for the collect, back to nadir after release.

orbit_intent.note: One circular 900 km orbit, derived and time-remapped: over 22.2 N 2.6 W at frame 146 heading 060. The shot spends its frames unevenly along the circle -- 2.4 degrees of arc per frame while the platform is behind the planet and coming round the limb, easing over frames 60-110 to 0.03 degrees per frame, where it stays. Solved with hero/scripts/orbit_plan.py against the R3 camera: hidden at the open, emerges from behind the lower-left limb near frame 58, climbs the limb while the camera completes its handover, and from frame 136 holds at about (0.25, 0.40) of the frame -- lower-left of the target, Earth right-dominant -- through the lock, the sweep and the release, because the camera is locked off for the same frames. The dive then leaves it behind: it exits the left edge near frame 204 at under 17 percent of the frame width and is never a foreground fly-by. Every hero orbit is time-compressed by orders of magnitude; the profile only lets that compression vary across the shot.

objects.yaw_note: Yaw about nadir so the array axis crosses the line of sight during the pass; with the arrays perpendicular to the orbit plane the wings pointed straight at the camera and the platform collapsed to a dot at review size.

objects.note: Subtle orbital trail: a ribbon on the derived orbit circle showing a fading window of arc behind the satellite. Secondary by construction (thin, faint, fades before the hold) and occluded by the planet exactly where the satellite is.

WEB-005A R3: the accepted 36 x 36 km analysis AOI as the frame the dive resolves onto. Same construction as the regional frame (parented to the Earth, geometry from the fixture through aoi_system.py), no sensing lines of its own: the border, corner locks and halo draw in at 236-254 with a lock pulse as the regional frame vanishes, a quick sweep seals it at 248-264, and it settles by 268 for the page-layer handoff. The audit publishes its last-frame screen corners as the handoff anchor. Nothing scientific is rendered into it.

aoi_beam.note: Sensing-line core: thin, crisp, visibly connected root to target; tapers toward the footprint but never below half opacity.

earth_surface.note: R3 albedo stack. Global: NASA Blue Marble Next Generation July 2004 with topography and bathymetry, 21600 x 10800. Regional: a lossless 8160 x 5520 crop of the 500 m C1 tile of the same dataset covering lon 12-46 E, lat 27-50 N, blended in over a 2.5 degree feather. Under the hold: a 30 m Sentinel-2 detail multiplier (window lon 28.15-29.42 E, lat 36.94-38.84 N) that carries ground structure without colour. Clouds: the NASA Blue Marble 8192 cloud composite mixed on top. sea_tint pulls open water toward the accepted darker navy from an albedo-derived mask. Presentation only: none of it is a measured layer and none of it moves the accepted target registration.

detail_sharpen.note: WEB-005A R3 regional detail multiplier (hero/scripts/materialize_earth_sharpen.py, record hero/evidence/earth_detail_sharpen.json): Sentinel-2 L2A 30 m broadband reflectance divided by its own 510 m blur, so the Blue Marble colour is kept everywhere and only the ground structure under the hold is added. Presentation only; not a measured layer.
detail_sharpen.feather_note: 0.28 degrees is about 25 km: wide enough that the step from 30 m structure to the 500 m Blue Marble window reads as depth of detail falling away, never as an edge. The analysis AOI (18 km half-span) sits wholly inside the full-strength region.

aoi_cone.note: Secondary support only: a broad, very faint volume under the lines.

aoi_border_analysis.note: Analysis-frame border: same look as aoi_border on its own datablock, so its appearance and lock pulse are keyed independently of the regional frame's vanish.

lighting_isolation.note: Cycles light linking: the primary sun keeps lighting everything but the satellite and only the planet blocks it; a duplicate sun lights only the satellite with its own parts as blockers. The body self-shadows (volumetric read) and never prints a shadow on the Earth.

glare.note: Controlled halo for the emissive frame, corner locks and sensing lines. The threshold sits above anything sunlit on the planet.

hero_r3_preview_gate.description: WEB-005A R3 preview gate (fixed-camera acquisition, scan fan, persistent lock frame, DEM-relief analytical reveal). Low-cost review scene required by tasks/WEB-005A_R3_REVIEW_37152222.md before any further long production render; it does not replace hero_production_kizildere, whose shipped media stay bound to their own configuration until Product passes this gate. One world, one camera, no cut: the observer is locked off from frame 1 until the scan fan and the four sensing lines have retired (208); the satellite alone moves, comes round the left limb and settles left-of-centre clear of the hero copy; four lines lock the corners of the presented lock frame, a translucent fan spans them and a light curtain sweeps the footprint left to right; only then does the camera approach, while the same frame tightens continuously onto the true 36 km footprint; at the hold the governed DEM lifts the footprint into relief and the prepared Terrain, THM-01, ALT-01 and priority display textures are revealed on that one registered surface, ending on priority alone.

render_overrides.note: The scan curtain is a stack of translucent slices; a view ray can cross most of them.

animation.continuity_note: Fixed observer 1-208: no camera key changes value before 208 and the AOI track constraint is off, so the only things that move are the satellite and the turning Earth. Lines connect 106-120, the frame locks 112-150, the fan rises 138-150, the curtain crosses west to east 148-194, fan, fill and lines retire 194-208. Approach 208-276 onto the hold; the lock frame morphs 208-276. Relief rises 284-308 and the four display textures cross-fade on it; from 398 only the priority layer remains.

shot_intent.note: Fixed observer (A-HERO-15): the opening state IS the acquisition state.
The accepted R3 acquisition composition, now held from frame 1: Earth right-dominant, left limb in frame for the satellite to come round, the target right-of-centre.
Hold: about 160 km across the frame at 36 deg incidence, oblique enough for the DEM relief to read; the 36 km footprint spans about 24 percent of the width in the right-middle zone.

track.note: Off for the whole fixed-observer phase: a track constraint would turn the camera with the Earth. The keyed aim at 208 already points at the AOI centre, so the hand-over cannot swing.

camera.shift_note: Constant through the fixed phase (a lens-shift change is apparent camera motion). Target at (0.77, 0.60) while acquiring, easing to (0.70, 0.52) -- right-middle -- at the hold.

copy_safe_region_1440.note: Measured in the built page at 1440 x 900: the hero is 1425 x 738 CSS px and the right edge of the widest copy line is 674 px, 0.473 of the hero width. The 16:9 media is cover-fitted at full width there, so a frame x is a page x.

presentation.purpose: One persistent lock frame. The authoritative footprint is the fixture (36 km) and is never edited; what is drawn around it is sized in screen space and tightens onto it.

scan_fan.note: Secondary support for the four lines: a faint veil on the four faces of the pyramid they span, and a light curtain -- a stack of translucent slices from the platform to the ground, lit only near the sweep position -- that crosses the footprint west to east in step with the ground band, because both read the same keyed sweep value.

objects.note: WEB-005A R3 persistent lock frame on the accepted 36 km analysis fixture.

orbit_intent.note: One circular 900 km orbit, derived and time-remapped, solved against the locked-off camera: over 23.76 N 19.81 E at frame 120 heading 100, which puts the platform at about (0.555, 0.38) of the frame -- left of centre, right of the hero copy column -- for the whole acquisition. 2.2 degrees of arc per frame while it is behind the planet and coming round the left limb, easing over 52-104 to 0.015, where it stays: with the observer fixed there is no parallax to hide a drift, so the platform creeps about two percent of the frame width through the beat and reads as station-keeping.

objects.yaw_note: Yaw about nadir so the array axis lies across the screen under the locked-off camera: the sun-tracking arrays then present about half their face to the observer instead of their edge.

objects.note: A-HERO-18/19. Geometry is displaced from the governed top-dem.tif only (never from a coloured texture), on the same fixture mapping the lock frame is drawn from; 3x is a presentation exaggeration, not a claim. The four prepared display textures are material only and share one UV.

aoi_fan_veil.note: Fan faces: invisible at the platform, a breath of cyan at the ground. Never a slab.

aoi_relief_layers.note: Prepared display textures, consumed byte-for-byte (checksums in hero/assets/manifest.json). No recolouring: the only thing the material adds is the scene's own light on the DEM relief.

aoi_relief_wall.note: Sides of the raised block: not ground and not data. A cyan glass that is absent at the globe and strongest at the rim, so the relief reads as the footprint lifted for analysis rather than as a slab with painted edges.

data_state_note: WEB-005 is the authorized integration gate. The four accepted WEB-HERO-001 scenes stay pre-data and unedited; the production scene binds accepted GEO-WEB-002 geometry and declares -- but does not bake -- the accepted result layer, which is composited in the page over the render so its governed pixels are never re-encoded. WEB-005A R2 revises only the production scene's visual treatment, camera composition, satellite and Earth albedo sources.
palette_note: beam_core, beam_glow and aoi_frame are the Product R2 hero FX lock (#7FEFFF, #3CCBFF, #98F5FF) converted from sRGB to linear.
